facts.fact: Under IGNOAPS (part of NSAP), persons aged 60 or above get central assistance of Rs 200 a month at ages 60-79
facts.quote: National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) – Persons aged 60 years and above. ₹200 per month (60–79 years) ₹500 per month (80 years and above)

facts.fact: From age 80 it is Rs 500 a month
facts.quote: The Ministry of Rural Development has informed that under IGNOAPS, financial assistance of ₹200 per month is provided to persons aged 60–79 years and ₹500 per month to persons aged 80 years and above, subject to eligibility under the Below Poverty Line (BPL) criteria.
facts.note: PIB release 2226202 posted 11 FEB 2026 (11.02.2026): written reply in the Rajya Sabha by the MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment.

facts.fact: It is for persons from BPL households
facts.quote: The assistance under the sub-schemes of NSAP are applicable for persons belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.

facts.fact: States/UTs add their own top-up from their own resources, so the total received differs by State
facts.quote: Under IGNOAPS, States/UTs are encouraged to provide top-up assistance from their own resources.

facts.fact: It is not limited to one person per family: every person aged 60+ in a BPL family is eligible
facts.quote: No. All the persons who are 60 years of age in a BPL family are eligible to get old age pension.

facts.fact: Payment is by Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)
facts.quote: NSAP delivers financial assistance through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism. Funds are credited directly into beneficiary accounts

facts.fact: Applications go to the State/UT department that implements NSAP (mostly the Social Welfare Department)
facts.quote: The NSAP Schemes are mainly implemented by the Social Welfare Departments in the States.

facts.fact: Locally the scheme is run through the Gram Panchayat or Municipality
facts.quote: At the local level, the Gram Panchayat /Municipality would implement the programmes.

summary: IGNOAPS Rs 200 (60-79) / Rs 500 (80+), BPL, State top-up, all 60+ in a BPL family, DBT and State-department route confirmed on NSAP About Us, FAQ, 2014 guidelines and the PIB Rajya Sabha reply (11.02.2026); no revision found.
